findings.description: The requirement combines retention of the latch, fault history, fault count and per-code detection counts; any one of those can be lost while the others are retained. SYS-SAFE-009 and SYS-SAFE-020 through SYS-SAFE-022 specify these separately.
findings.requested_change: Limit this requirement to latch retention and leave the other retention obligations to the separately stated requirements.

findings.description: The requirement says the software loses the latch and counts at loss of power, although software cannot act while unpowered. It also says each count starts at zero after power-on reset without ordering initialization before new events, which can erase start-up detections or reports required by SWR-SAFE-027 and SWR-SAFE-028. SYS-SAFE-013 instead specifies clearing the prior latch at power-on reset without preventing it from being set again.
findings.requested_change: State the software obligation at power-on reset in line with SYS-SAFE-013, preserving later latch events, and leave history and count initialization to the separate requirements.

findings.description: Loss of the latch, fault history, fault count and per-code detection counts are independently judgeable obligations. The system requirements split these behaviors between SYS-SAFE-013 and SYS-SAFE-024 through SYS-SAFE-027.
findings.requested_change: Restrict this requirement to the prior safe-state latch and rely on the separate requirements for fault history and count initialization.
